properties.statement: THE TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT WOULD REVEAL AN UNPOPULATED DECOMPOSITION BOTH REPORT SUCCESS. Measured 2026-08-07 on reflow2's own design while answering Anthony's question about recursive black-box decomposition. (1) evaluate_allocation returns modularity 1.0 with total_external 0 and total_internal 1 — a PERFECT modularity score computed over exactly ONE dependency. Every one of the 44 listed components reports external_weight 0 and internal_weight 0. The graph holds 171 DEPENDS_ON edges; the allocation evaluator sees one, so the metric is structurally starved and the number it prints is 1/1. graph_report_markdown renders this as "Allocation health: Modularity 1.00 across 44 component(s); 0 misplaced capability(ies). No god-components." (2) hierarchy_issues returns count 0 on a hierarchy that is TWO levels deep and INCOMPLETE: 8 subsystems contain 42 components, and 6 ordinary components sit outside every subsystem — 14 component roots in total. Neither the shallowness nor the six orphans is reported. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN EITHER NUMBER: req:recursive-black-box-decomposition is original intent — Anthony's words, "one of the primary things I designed it for" — and the reason it went unnoticed is that the design's own health readout says the decomposition is perfect. This is the exact pattern the standing feedback names: a green gate is the weakest evidence in the building, and 0 gaps / 0 defects / loop clean held throughout eleven releases in which ten schema domains were invisible. Here the same shape appears one layer in: the allocation analysis cannot distinguish a well-modularised design from one with almost no modelled dependencies, and reports the second as the first. THE COMPANION MEASUREMENT, which is the real hole: 5 Interface nodes and 5 PROVIDES / 5 CONSUMES edges for 56 components. The trajectory already reports this honestly as seams 0% (0/73) and calls it the frontier — so the SEAM metric is candid where the ALLOCATION metric is not, about the same underlying emptiness. NOT A REQUEST TO CHANGE THE MODULARITY FORMULA: dec:report-dont-judge is deliberate and granularity_report's refusal to rule is right. What is wrong is a metric reporting a value at all when its denominator is one, instead of saying it has too little to measure — the same distinction dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked already raises for unsurfaced_gaps, where "clean" and "never scanned" are the same answer.
